title: because
gist: I ran preregistered experiments on what makes Claude Code follow its instructions. In an exploratory comparison, which rule you write and whether you write it at all matter far more than how you word it, and past a fixed budget the skill listing drops long descriptions before the model reads them.
summary: Tells you which edits to a CLAUDE.md or a skill description change what Claude Code does, with the data and the checkers to rerun every number.

hero_image.alt: Forest plot of wording effects on compliance, on an axis from -30 to +30 points. All estimates sit within 4.3 points of zero.

site.eyebrow: Preregistered experiments · three studies · Claude Code 2.1.303 · MIT
site.blurb: I ran three preregistered experiments on what makes Claude Code follow its instructions. In an exploratory comparison, which rule you write and whether you write it at all matter far more than wording, and past a 30,000 character budget the skill listing drops long descriptions, so a short one beats a long trigger list by 29.8 points at 300 skills. Giving a reason, the question I went in for, reads as inconclusive at +0.2 points [-5.2, +5.7].
